name: Adani Power Ltd
title: Adani Power Ltd - 533096 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Adani Power's Q4 FY26 PLF was 74% and FY26 PLF 66.5%, with 95% of operating capacity tied to PPAs and capex guided to INR25,000 crore in FY27, though Mahan and Korba timelines slipped and merchant exposure fell to 5%.

triggers.quote: Peak demand has recently reached 256 gigawatts, and it is expected to rise further in the current year.

triggers.label: Merchant share 16% → 5%

summary.headline: Adani Power Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA rose 27% YoY to INR6,498 crore and PAT 64% to INR4,271 crore, though continuing EBITDA grew only 9%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of INR6,498 crore (up 27% YoY) and PAT of INR4,271 crore (up 64% YoY), but continuing EBITDA was INR5,573 crore (up 9%), with the gap tied to recently acquired assets and PPA-related items. Full-year FY26 continuing revenue was INR55,583 crore and continuing EBITDA INR21,285 crore, both broadly flat, as weak merchant prices and lower imported-coal tariffs offset volume growth. Management reported 95% of 18.15 GW operating capacity under long- or medium-term PPAs, with merchant exposure cut from 16% to about 5%. Expansion remains on plan with a 1.32 GW Korba Phase-II and a 1.6 GW Mahan Phase-II timeline, though Mahan has been pushed toward FY28 on geopolitical labour and LPG constraints. Net debt rose to INR45,022 crore on bridge financing for capex.

segments.name: Operations (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Q4 PLF 74%, FY26 PLF 66.5%; Q4 power sales 27.2 BU and FY26 sales 99.1 BU (+3.4%). Plant availability above 91% in Q1 FY27 vs ~88% a year earlier.

segments.name: Merchant exposure
segments.commentary: Open merchant capacity is about 5% (roughly 1 GW), down from 16% at the start of FY26; remaining open capacity sits mainly at Mundra Unit 9, Mahan Stage 1 and a small part of Raipur.

guidance_outlook: Korba Phase-II (1.32 GW): Unit 1 in Q2 FY27, Unit 2 before year-end FY27; estimated FY27 EBITDA contribution about INR1,000 crore, rising in FY28 on a full-year basis.
Mahan Phase-II (1.6 GW): first unit targeted by end-FY27, at the latest Q1 FY28, second unit about six months later; slippage attributed to labour and LPG availability.
Capex about INR25,000 crore in FY27 and about INR33,000 crore in FY28, within an INR2 lakh crore expansion plan; annualised FFO about INR20,000 crore.
Management targets about INR50,000 crore EBITDA by FY31 conservatively, possibly 2030; capacity of 42 GW targeted by FY31-32, with debt repayment largely complete by FY31-32.
Commissioning deferrals average about 6 months, with 4 GW or more per year planned from FY29 to FY32; management says the 34 GW-by-2030 plan remains on track.

Maharashtra 1,600 MW PPA (INR5.30/unit: INR4.11 capacity, INR1.19 energy): PPA signing expected within about 3 months; commissioning 4-5 years out, with project location (Raigarh, Raipur or Korba) not yet assigned.
capex_capacity: Expansion: 23.7 GW thermal targeted by 2032; 13.3 GW of long-term PPAs tied up for expansion after the 1,600 MW Maharashtra LoA.
Under-construction progress: Mahan Phase-II 86%, Raipur Phase-II 54%, Raigarh Phase-II 47%; Korba Phase-II close to completion.
Korba total capex about INR8,000-8,500 crore including about INR4,100 crore acquisition cost, with a further about INR4,000 crore to spend.
Operating capacity 18.15 GW; operating capacity rose only about 600 MW YoY as Vidarbha acquired assets and expansion CWIP were added to fixed assets.
Nuclear: several SPVs incorporated, all new sites, awaiting government rules before deciding size and technology; Bhutan 570 MW hydro SPV incorporated.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew 0.8% in FY26 and 1.6% in Q4 FY26; demand revived from March, with peak demand recently reaching 256 GW.
Merchant prices were subdued through most of FY26 with a weak merchant realisation; management cited prices ranging from INR3 to INR7-8 per unit depending on weather.
PPA tariffs for imported-coal plants fell with lower import coal prices; fuel cost is a pass-through under PPAs.
About 13 GW of PPAs in the market across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Gujarat, plus about 4 GW new Gujarat tender.
Domestic coal supply not affected by the geopolitical situation; imported-coal shipping costs up, but pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Maharashtra 1,600 MW PPA: which project and what tariff?
qa_highlights.answer: Location not yet assigned (Raigarh, Raipur or Korba); tariff INR5.30/unit, of which INR4.11 capacity and INR1.19 energy.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and funding for FY27-28, and Korba/Mahan timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR25,000 crore in FY27 and INR33,000 crore in FY28; Korba Unit 1 in Q2 FY27, Mahan Unit 1 by end-FY27 at the latest Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Mahan (1.6 GW) pushed out from this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Conservative stance due to labour and LPG availability under the geopolitical situation; one unit still targeted by end-FY27, with Q1 FY28 as the fallback.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of borrowing after the debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Recent market borrowing cost about 8%, via domestic capital market (DCM) or domestic banks.

qa_highlights.question: Non-controlling interest jumped from INR8.5 crore in Q3 to INR254 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by Moxie Power Unit 2 medium-term PPA with Tamil Nadu (558 MW) starting in Q4; full 12-month consolidation of Coastal Energen also added to the year-on-year rise.

qa_highlights.question: Has the group signed a long-term PPA for merchant capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No group PPA signed during FY26; the 1,600 MW Maharashtra PPA is being served via a trading platform for residual capacity, including renewables and storage.

risks_watch: Merchant price volatility: prices range widely with weather and rising renewables, and management expects merchant prices to fall over time.
Execution risk on Mahan and Korba timelines given labour and LPG constraints linked to the geopolitical situation.
Leverage: net debt INR45,022 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and borrowing cost near 8%, with the expansion funded by interim debt before internal accruals.
Q1 FY27 PLF is lower YoY (74%) due to weak merchant prices; management expects better PLF through FY27.
Bangladesh PBDB receivable: outstanding has fallen and payments are regular, but the disputed amount remains with an expert, with possible SIAC arbitration.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and PPA visibility, but cautious and conservative on near-term commissioning dates, attributing deferrals to geopolitical labour and LPG constraints. Several answers on merchant pricing and on the reasons for the Q-o-Q non-controlling interest jump were non-committal or required follow-up.
key_quotes: We are making excellent progress towards our goal of adding 23.7 gigawatts of thermal capacity by 2032.
95% of our operating capacity of 18.15 gigawatts is now tied up under long-term and medium-term PPAs.
So, we are confident that by FY31-32 our capacity will be 42 gigawatt from a planned capacity.
Our Q4 power sales reached 27.2 billion unit, while full year sales increased 3.4% to 99.1 billion unit.

growth.why: Management guides to EBITDA of INR50,000 crore by FY31 and 42 GW by FY31-32, backed by Korba Phase-II (1.32 GW, Unit 1 Q2 FY27) and Mahan Phase-II (1.6 GW, end-FY27 to Q1 FY28), but Mahan has slipped and the FY26 continuing revenue and EBITDA were flat, so near-term growth rests mainly on capacity additions and FY27 capex of about INR25,000 crore.
